ai.literal: Even if you conceal, transgressing the limit and refusing to cooperate, your kohl-dyed eyes, to speak, that which they intend, one thing, there is.
ai.translation: Even if you try to hide your feelings, going beyond all limits of self-control and refusing to cooperate, there is something that your kohl-dyed eyes are trying to say.
ai.modern: நீ மறைக்க முயன்றாலும், எல்லை கடந்து உனக்கு அடங்காமல், உன்னுடைய மை தீட்டிய கண்கள் சொல்ல விரும்பும் செய்தி ஒன்று இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the speaker observes that the lady is trying hard to conceal her inner feelings of love or longing. However, her beautiful, kohl-dyed eyes ('உண்கண்') refuse to cooperate with her attempt at secrecy. They have transgressed the limits of her self-control ('கை இகந்து ஒல்லா') and are visibly eager to reveal the truth. The speaker gently points out that there is indeed a message ('உரைக்கல் உறுவது ஒன்று உண்டு') written clearly in her gaze.

ai.literal: For the simple woman who has eye-filling beauty and bamboo-resembling shoulders, her womanhood-filled modesty is great.
ai.translation: For this simple maiden of eye-filling beauty and bamboo-like shoulders, her abundant feminine modesty is indeed great.
ai.modern: கண்களை நிறைக்கும் அழகுடைய, மூங்கில் போன்ற தோள்களைக் கொண்ட இந்தப் பெண்ணிடம், பெண்மை நிறைந்த குணங்கள் மிக அதிகமாக உள்ளன.
ai.explanation: The hero admires the heroine's self-control and modesty. While she possesses eye-filling beauty ('கண்ணிறைந்த காரிகை') and beautiful shoulders resembling smooth bamboo ('காம்பேர்தோள்'), her feminine modesty and reserve ('பெண் நிறைந்த நீர்மை') are even more prominent. She does not easily betray her inner feelings, showing a dignified restraint that makes her even more attractive.

ai.literal: Like the thread that shines within a gem, there is one thing that shines within the ornaments of this young woman.
ai.translation: Like the thread that shows through a translucent gem, there is a hidden feeling that shines through this young woman's beauty.
ai.modern: பளிங்கு மணியின் உள்ளே விளங்கும் நூலைப் போல, இந்தப் பெண்ணின் அழகிற்குள்ளே விளங்குகின்ற குறிப்பு ஒன்று இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful simile to describe how a woman's inner feelings are revealed. Just as a thread passing through a semi-transparent bead is visible from the outside, there is an underlying emotion—her love or desire—that shines through her physical beauty and ornaments. The word 'maṭantai' refers to a young woman, and 'aṇi' means her ornaments or physical grace. The speaker observes that her outer appearance does not completely hide her inner heart; rather, her true feelings are subtly yet clearly visible to those who look closely.

ai.literal: Like the fragrance that is inside a flower bud, there is something inside the budding smile of this innocent woman.
ai.translation: Like the fragrance hidden within an unopened flower bud, there is a secret meaning concealed within the budding smile of this innocent maid.
ai.modern: பூ மொட்டின் உள்ளே இருக்கும் நறுமணத்தைப் போல, இந்தப் பேதைப் பெண்ணின் அரும்பும் புன்னகைக்குள் ஏதோ ஒரு குறிப்பு ஒளிந்திருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover reads the subtle signs of his beloved's feelings. He compares her gentle, half-formed smile to a tight flower bud. Just as a bud holds its sweet fragrance secretly inside before blooming, her budding smile carries a hidden thought or message. The word 'nāṟṟam' is used here in its classical sense of sweet fragrance, and 'pētai' highlights her innocence. This beautiful metaphor shows how her unspoken love is felt even before it is openly expressed.

ai.literal: She of tight bangles having practiced exceeding feigned-indifference, intense-grief curing remedy one possesses.
ai.translation: The excessive, feigned indifference shown by her who wears tight-fitting bangles contains within itself a remedy to cure the very grief it causes.
ai.modern: நெருக்கமான வளையல்களை அணிந்தவள் எல்லை கடந்து செய்த பொய்க் கோபம், அதனால் உண்டாகும் மிகுந்த துன்பத்தைத் தீர்க்கும் ஒரு மருந்தையும் தன்னுள் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover speaks of his beloved's playful avoidance or feigned anger, referred to as 'kaḷḷam' (deceit or pretense). She is described as wearing tight-fitting bangles ('ceṟitoṭi'), and her mock indifference has exceeded normal limits. Although this behavior causes him intense grief ('uṟutuyar'), he realizes that her playful pretense actually contains the remedy ('maruntu') to cure his distress. The remedy is her underlying love, which will soon reveal itself and bring him joy.

ai.literal: Greatly comforting and lovingly uniting, (and then) with difficulty enduring, possesses the nature of planning an absence of love.
ai.translation: His excessive comforting and loving embrace, followed by a strained, difficult endurance, reveals a hidden design to depart, showing a lack of love.
ai.modern: மிகவும் ஆறுதல் கூறி அன்போடு கூடுதல், பின்னர் பிரிவைத் தாங்குவது போல வருந்துதல் ஆகிய இரண்டும், என்னைப் பிரிய நினைக்கும் அன்பில்லாத தன்மையைக் குறிப்பதாகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine reads the subtle behavioral signs of her lover. She notices that his sudden, unusually intense affection and comforting embrace are followed by a strained, difficult endurance. She realizes that this dramatic shift in behavior is not just ordinary affection, but a sign that he is mentally preparing himself for separation. Thus, she concludes that his actions betray a plan to leave her, which she views as a lack of true love.

ai.literal: The cool shore's lord's departure, even before us, beforehand sensed, the bangles.
ai.translation: Even before I could fully realize that the lord of the cool shore had departed, my slipping bangles sensed it first.
ai.modern: குளிர்ந்த கடற்கரைத் தலைவன் நம்மைப் பிரிந்து சென்றதை, நம்மை விட முன்னதாகவே என் கைகளில் உள்ள வளையல்கள் உணர்ந்து கொண்டு கழன்றன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks of her deep grief over her lover's departure. The lover is addressed as the lord of the cool maritime shore (துறைவன்). Even before her mind could fully process the pain of his separation (நம்மினும் முன்னம் உணர்ந்த), her body reacted instantly to the sorrow. Her arms grew thin from grief, causing her bangles (வளை) to slip off, making it seem as though the bangles knew of the departure before she herself did.

ai.literal: Yesterday departed my lover; and I, seven days we are, body having turned pale.
ai.translation: It was only yesterday that my lover departed; yet, my body has been pale with grief for seven days now.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் நேற்றுத்தான் பிரிந்து சென்றார்; ஆனால், என் உடலோ பசலை நோய் வந்து ஏழு நாட்கள் ஆனது போலப் பசந்து போய்விட்டது.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks of her intense longing and the distortion of time in her lover's absence. He left only yesterday, but her body has already turned pale with the grief of separation (pasalai). To her suffering mind, this physical change makes it feel as though seven long days have already passed. The couplet beautifully contrasts the objective reality of time with the subjective experience of pain.

ai.literal: Looking at her bracelet, looking also at her soft shoulders, looking at her feet, that was what she did there.
ai.translation: She looked at her bracelets, she looked at her soft shoulders, and she looked down at her feet; that was all she did there.
ai.modern: தன் வளையல்களைப் பார்த்து, தன் மென்மையான தோள்களையும் பார்த்து, தன் பாதங்களையும் பார்த்தாள்; அவள் அங்கு செய்தது அதுவே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the hero interprets the silent, expressive gestures of his beloved. By looking at her bracelets ('toṭi'), she hints at her fear that they will grow loose and fall off due to the physical wasting caused by separation. Her gaze at her soft shoulders ('mentōḷ') expresses concern that they will lose their fullness, and looking down at her feet ('aṭi') signals her desire to accompany him. Through these three quiet glances, she communicates her deep anxiety about his impending departure without uttering a single word.

ai.literal: They say that begging, by expressing the pain of love through the eyes, possesses a femininity greater than womanhood itself.
ai.translation: They say that pleading for love by silently expressing one's love-sickness through the eyes possesses a grace far greater than womanhood itself.
ai.modern: கண்களால் காம நோயைக் கூறி இரந்து நிற்பது, பெண்ணியல்பைக் காட்டிலும் மிகுந்த பெண்மைத் தன்மையைக் கொண்டது என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme beauty of feminine modesty in love. Instead of expressing her deep longing and love-sickness in words, the heroine conveys it subtly through her eyes. The act of pleading for her lover's union solely through her gaze is described as possessing a grace that surpasses even womanhood itself. The word 'iravu' here refers to the silent begging or pleading for love, and 'peṇmai' represents the ideal quality of feminine reserve and beauty.
